coverage.summary: The only source is a secondary table row. It states no limits on which buildings, units or landlords are covered and describes the prohibition as applying to landlords generally. Any exemptions or size thresholds in the actual ordinance are unknown.

evidence.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using algorithmic devices and shared competitor information to set rent, fees, or other rental terms.

result.notes: The only source is a secondary law-firm table row. It gives no unit thresholds, construction dates, owner-occupancy exemptions, landlord-size conditions or preemption language for Rockville. I left all of those null. The row describes a general prohibition on landlords, so requires_unknown_facts is set to false. Scope should be verified against the official Rockville City Code § 18-148. The source shows that other ordinances in the same table have owner-size limits (for example, Portland's 16-or-more-unit limit on private remedies), so Rockville's ordinance may also contain limits the source does not report.
